diagnosis: WNT-activated deep penetrating / plexiform melanocytoma (naevus), plexiform spindle cell pattern
legend: Pigmented and spindled melanocytes are centred on the cutaneous vascular plexus, assuming a plexiform (candelabra-like) architectural configuration.

diagnosis: WNT-activated deep penetrating / plexiform melanocytoma (naevus), deep penetrating subtype

legend: Bundles of melanocytes showing nuclear positivity for β-catenin immunostaining, among conventional naevus melanocytes devoid of nuclear expression.
β-catenin immunohistochemistry with a red substrate to distinguish positive expression from melanin. Positive nuclear β-catenin highlights a plexiform architecture of the proliferation.

Slightly enlarged fusiform melanocytes are arranged in bundles. These melanocytes contain scant, finely granular, greyish-brown cytoplasmic melanin, as well as enlarged nuclei with slight pleomorphism (haematoxylin phloxine saffron stain).

diagnosis: WNT-activated deep penetrating / plexiform melanocytoma (naevus), plexiform spindle cell subtype
legend: Fascicles of melanocytes with scattered melanophages infiltrate the deep dermis (haematoxylin phloxine saffron stain).

diagnosis: WNT-activated deep penetrating / plexiform melanocytoma (naevus), plexiform spindle cell subtype
legend: Fascicles of melanocytes can extend along adnexal structures (haematoxylin phloxine saffron stain).

Bundles with slightly enlarged melanocytes with little pleomorphism are present among sheets of bland cells of a conventional dermal naevus, separated by scattered melanophages (haematoxylin phloxine saffron stain).
Bundles of melanocytes are present among sheets of a conventional dermal naevus (haematoxylin phloxine saffron stain).

β-catenin immunohistochemistry with a red substrate to distinguish positive expression from melanin. The melanocytes show a cytoplasmic and nuclear staining. Internal control is represented by a hair follicle without nuclear staining.

diagnosis: WNT-activated deep penetrating / plexiform melanocytoma (naevus), deep penetrating subtype
legend: Slightly enlarged melanocytes are arranged in fascicles or bundles, associated with some melanophages. The melanocytes have a finely granular pigmented cytoplasm and present some degree of atypia.
A pigmented nodule that is generally symmetrical and not ulcerated. Biopsy and histopathological examination are required to distinguish this lesion from a nodular melanoma.
